independent.summary: LEO-067's stated measurement is wrong: in the installed mongoose 8.23, `lib/cast/string.js` throws CastError for arrays too (`value.toString && ... && !Array.isArray(value)`), so `?domain=a&domain=b` is a second public crash vector the item describes as casting fine — an implementer encoding "array casts fine" as a test expectation would get a red test.

LEO-071 scopes `crawlSettings.honorRobots` as a flag "Daniel turns on for one entity" but lists no UI/API path to set it: `dashboard/src/views/Settings.vue:42-47` builds crawlSettings from an explicit 4-key whitelist and `dashboard.js:310` `findOneAndUpdate` $sets the subdocument wholesale, so a flag set out-of-band is silently reset the next time any owner saves settings.

The item attributes the crash to "Node 24's default" while the deployed runtime is pinned to nodejs_20 in the root `nixpacks.toml` — the conclusion still holds (throw-on-unhandled-rejection has been the default since Node 15), but the environment claim is wrong and a reader checking the pin could wrongly dismiss the item.

grades.reason: A `try`/`catch` inside each handler body means the promise never rejects unhandled, so it is the root-cause fix; `backend/index.js` is denylisted and the item explicitly puts process-level handlers out of scope, with the test registering `unhandledRejection` as the proof gate.

The diff itself states in bold that `backend/index.js` is denylisted and the six wiring lines are Daniel's by hand, and the item is tagged `[needs-human]` under `## Proposed` where selection skips it — restating the diff's own disclosure is not a defect.

summary: Both local findings restate limitations the diff already discloses and one misunderstands that in-handler try/catch is itself the fix, while the three verifiable factual gaps in the filed specs (mongoose array cast, unreachable honorRobots flag, wrong Node pin) went unnoticed.
